sections.title: Storage Class Transitions, Lifecycle Rules, and S3 Analytics
sections.objective: Design lifecycle configurations that transition, expire, or clean up objects by prefix or tag, and decide when S3 Storage Class Analysis is a valid input to those rules.

sections.title: Requester Pays and S3 Event Notifications
sections.objective: Choose between native S3 event notifications and EventBridge for event-driven integration, and identify the IAM permissions and authentication constraints each option requires.

sections.title: S3 Performance: Baseline Throughput, Multi-Part Upload, Transfer Acceleration, Byte-Range Fetches
sections.objective: Select S3 performance features and prefix strategies that meet a stated throughput, upload speed, or download resilience requirement.

sections.title: S3 Batch Operations and S3 Storage Lens
sections.objective: Match bulk object operations and Storage Lens metric categories to a given cost-optimization, data-protection, or governance scenario.

notes: Scope follows the chapter's sub-headings; page 294 is the title slide and adds no examinable content. Exam weighting: lifecycle rules and Storage Class Analysis support Task 4.1 (managing S3 object lifecycles, selecting storage tiers); multi-part upload, Transfer Acceleration, byte-range fetches, and prefix throughput support Task 3.1 (storage configurations meeting performance demands); S3 event notifications and EventBridge support Task 2.1 (event-driven architectures). Requester Pays appears explicitly in Task 4.1 as a cost-optimization access option. Common distractors to expect: Storage Class Analysis for One-Zone IA or Glacier (unsupported), anonymous Requester Pays access (not allowed), byte-range fetches used for uploads, and Standard IA chosen where Glacier retrieval time is acceptable. Background (tutor-supplied): event notification delivery is not guaranteed and events can occasionally arrive out of order, so exams favor designs that tolerate at-least-once delivery.
